title: Tool provenance handshake and stream ACK protocol for OpenAI-compatible toolcalls
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: OpenAI-style function/tool calling is flexible but fragile in streaming scenarios and through proxies (edge load balancers, gateways, SDK shims). We observed two classes of problems: (1) tool selection ambiguity when multiple compatible tool schemas exist (tool_choice semantics), and (2) stream fragmentation where tool-invoke frames are split or reordered, causing downstream tool agents to misinterpret or drop messages. This PR introduces a lightweight provenance handshake and an explicit stream-level ACK frame to make tool invocation deterministic and resilient across proxies and partial streams.

Design summary: single-line description: introduce a pre-invoke provenance handshake header and an in-stream ACK frame with idempotency tokens. Key behaviors implemented: 1) At dispatch, the router includes an x-rw-tool-provenance header encoding {tool_id, schema_id, schema_version, provenance_score} (base64-encoded JSON). This gives downstream workers an authoritative schema mapping and a provenance score used by deterministic tiebreakers. 2) We add a new framed streaming control message "tool_ack" that worker runtimes send back as soon as they accept the invocation and validate the inbound schema. The ack includes an idempotency token and a schema fingerprint. 3) If an ack is not observed within the configured ack_timeout, the caller receives a structured fallback event and the router can either (a) re-route to a pre-registered compatible tool, or (b) fall back to non-tool textual output per customer policy. 4) Fragment preservation: workers coalesce adjacent framed tool messages until the invocation is complete (terminal "tool_frag_end" frame). We added heuristics to reassemble fragmented JSON payloads and to signal a "fragment_repair" event if a fragment is missing after repair_timeout.

Compatibility and semantics: The changes are additive and opt-in: hosted OpenAI-compat adapter will emit x-rw-tool-provenance only when the call is detected as a tool/function invocation. Existing clients that ignore headers are unaffected; tool runtimes that haven’t been upgraded will still receive the original invoke envelope but will not emit tool_ack which triggers fallback behavior after ack_timeout. To preserve OpenAI compatibility, we do not change the visible JSON function schema in the final payload; the provenance header and tool_ack are transport-level signals only. The tool_choice tiebreak uses provenance_score + deterministic tie hash (request_id + elapsed_ms) to avoid non-deterministic selection under load.

Telemetry and observability: new metrics: rw_tool.ack.latency, rw_tool.ack.missing, rw_tool.fragment.repaired, rw_tool.choice.tiebreak.count. We added trace spans around handshake serialization and ack handling; these are surfaced in the Console per-route timeline and in the per-token breakdown for auditing.

Testing: unit tests for header encoding/decoding, ack frame serialization, and multiple fragment reassembly were added. Integration tests cover (a) proxy that strips and reorders frames, (b) worker that validates schema mismatch and returns an explicit reject ack, (c) rollback to fallback tool when ack missing. E2E staging runs simulated 1000 concurrent toolcalls with 50ms median ack latency and verified 99.95% success within ack_timeout.

Rollout plan: staged rollout: 1) internal canary on dedicated infra (1% of traffic) for 48h with enhanced telemetry, 2) opt-in customer beta for Hosted API, 3) default on for new OpenAI-compat v2 adapter and opt-out flag for customers needing older behavior. Migration notes: customers implementing custom tool runtimes should read the SDK guide; minimal change required: emit tool_ack on successful validation (SDKs updated in this PR to include helpers).

Checklist:
- [x] Header format spec added (docs/compat/tool-provenance.md)
- [x] Runtime ack frame implemented (runtime/streaming/ack.go)
- [x] SDK helper added (redwood-sdk-python/tool_ack.py)
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Telemetry + Console surfaces

Related: ENG-1123 (tool reliability), ENG-1178 (streaming fragmentation).

runtime: emit tool_ack frame on worker accept
sdk/python: add helper to emit ack and validate schema
streaming: fragment coalescer and repair heuristics
docs: add compat guide and rollout plan
review_comments: Evelyn Li: Nice incremental design. Two asks: add a short explanation for the deterministic tie hash and make ack_timeout configurable per-customer (not just global).
Author (Asha): Added configurable ack_timeout per-customer via routing config and documented deterministic tie hash in the spec (hash = sha256(request_id || schema_id) % 10000).
Marco Ruiz: Can we avoid the base64 JSON header to reduce header size? Consider compact binary fingerprinting.
Author (Asha): Switched to a compact fingerprint for schema_id and keep a short provenance byte mask; still include a base64 reference for debug mode. See runtime/streaming/ack.go changes.
Priya Nair: Tests look good. Please add a sanity test that asserts behavior when an older worker doesn't emit ack (fallback path).
Author (Asha): Added integration test proxy-old-worker-fallback.test and verified behavior in staging.
release_notes: Added a transport-level tool provenance header and an in-stream tool_ack frame to improve determinism and robustness of OpenAI-compatible tool/function calls. Enables deterministic tool_choice tiebreaking and fragment repair. Opt-in rollout; SDK helpers added.
short_summary: Adds provenance handshake and stream-level ACK to make toolcalls deterministic and tolerant to fragmenting proxies; includes SDK helpers, telemetry, and tests.
